examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Point on a Curve With a Certain Slope
examples.problem: Find the $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=3x^2+1$ where the tangent line has a slope of $-1.$
examples.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=3x^2+1.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to $f'(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}+1) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\  & =3\cdot 2x+0 \\  & =6x+0 \\  & =6x.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set $f'(x) = -1$ and solve for $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =-1 \\ 6x & =-1 \\ x & =-\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $-1$ at the point where $x=-\dfrac 1 6.$

feedback.worked_solution:
This time, we'll use $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x-2\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4x-2{x}^{1/2}) \\  & =4-2\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2} \\  & =4-\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=4$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4} & =4-\frac{1}{\sqrt{4}} \\  & =4-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,12)$ is

$$
m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4}=\frac{7}{2}.
$$
